gen-dafont-ethnocentric-general-sans: Ethnocentric looks fast and a little aggressive, with wide-spaced letters and short ascenders above big bowls. And General Sans follows in a sans-serif voice, its pressure steady and its tall x-height filling each line smoothly.
gen-dafont-galaxy-manrope: Galaxy goes cosmic, with loose, spacious letters in a dense band. Manrope keeps its sans curves bright and open at every mouth, so a long passage moves along easily with hardly any step between capitals and lowercase.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-switzer: Switzer reads like wire bent into letters, tall in the waist, with c tips that never drift toward touching. Jelly Crazies, with bowls nearly sealed shut, slows everything to a leisurely wobble.
gen-dafont-joystix-work-sans: Pure arcade swagger, widely tracked, with stems barely heavier than the arms linking them. Work Sans then steps in as a plain sans with joins as thick as its strokes; give Joystix the larger size and let the text sit smaller.
gen-dafont-junegull-archivo: Junegull draws every letter like one marker line, with lowercase as sturdy as cast iron capitals. Archivo, a sans-serif with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height, makes a long page feel editorial and welcoming.
gen-dafont-nasalization-fs-epilogue: Nasalization floats its big, short-ascendered letters well apart, friendly and a bit futuristic. But Epilogue, a plain sans with a wire-like monoline skeleton and curvy, unclamped shapes, fills the space below with a tall-bodied lowercase.
gen-dafont-nordic-fs-fira-sans: Nordic feels ancient, its monoweight strokes dabbed far apart with cramped openings. Fira Sans, a plain sans with wide-open s curves and a generous x-height, carries a long passage without any thick-thin flicker.
gen-dafont-nulshock-general-sans: General Sans reads smoothly, its pen pressure steady and its x-height filling the line. Nulshock, stretched and technical with an unshaded outline, wants the bigger size, while this sans-serif sits comfortably smaller beneath it.
gen-dafont-origami-switzer: Think sign-painter's brush at constant width, with a lowercase mass like poured lead. Switzer, a sans-serif of tubular, wire-like letters and tall waist line, gives the pair its best quality: weight above, wiry lightness below.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-epilogue: Epilogue draws a thread of ink with curvy, unclamped letters and stubby ascender tips. Starborn handles dreamy, spaced-out headline moments best, but this sans does the steady everyday work of carrying words with a tall lowercase.
